comments.author: vhantz
comments.textRawHtml:
Schrödinger's China at once is an evil entity looking to use AI for their own nefarious purposes yet also willing to cooperate with their main competitor to prevent other actors (who??) from achieving similar goals (all while under a chip embargo too!!)

The reality is much less confusing: Anthropic CEO does not wish for models with similar (or greater) capabilities compared to his own closed and overpriced ones to be widely released. Simply because that will affect Anthropic's bottom-line.

Anthropic and all other "model" companies have nothing making them special beyond privileged access to chips so obviously they want to restrict what models are out there and more importantly who can produce new ones. Without these restrictions, it's only a matter of time before the multi-hundred billions valuations simply evaporate while they are still holding the bag.
comments.textZhHtml:
薛定谔的中国，一方面被描绘成企图利用AI实现其险恶目的的邪恶实体，另一方面又被说成愿意与主要竞争对手合作，以阻止其他行为体（谁？？）实现类似目标（而且这一切还是在芯片禁运之下！！）

现实远没有那么令人困惑：Anthropic CEO只是不希望那些与其自家闭源且定价过高的模型能力相当（甚至更强）的模型被广泛发布。原因很简单，这会直接影响Anthropic的利润。

Anthropic和其他所有“模型”公司，除了享有获取芯片的特权外，根本没有什么特别之处，所以他们显然想要限制市面上有哪些模型，更重要的是限制谁能开发新模型。如果没有这些限制，他们还在高位站岗时，那数千亿美元的估值化为泡影就只是时间问题了。

He's also completely missed what many of us see as the primary the issue, HF was attacked by a US frontier model.

HF could not be helped by US frontier models because of the "safety" features they have.

HF had to use an open model from china.

Anthropic wants to add those "safety" features to open models - especially from china.

End result would be HF hack would have continued atleast until the Monday that OpenAI engineers finally walked back into work.
children.textZhHtml:
他还完全忽略了很多人认为的核心问题：HF遭到的是美国前沿模型的攻击。

由于所谓的“安全”功能，美国前沿模型根本无法向HF提供援助。

HF不得不使用来自中国的开源模型。

而Anthropic却想把这些“安全”功能强加给开源模型——尤其是来自中国的开源模型。

最终的结果就是，对HF的攻击至少会持续到 OpenAI 的工程师们周一终于回来上班的那一天。

children.author: Loquebantur
children.textRawHtml:
The public narrative around conspiracy theories is baffling for sure: what rational basis is there for assuming them wrong? Often none.

Incentive and ability are what should be looked at. There, things get far more interesting: what is the current state of AI employed by the US intelligence agencies and what do they use it for?

Having the public convinced, their "superiors" would only do everything in their best interest, even without anybody knowing for sure, is Huxley's Brave New World in real life.
children.textZhHtml:
围绕阴谋论的公众叙事确实令人费解：有什么理性依据能假定它们是错的呢？通常根本没有。

应该关注的是动机和能力。这样一来，事情就变得有趣多了：美国情报机构目前使用的AI处于什么状态，他们用它来做什么？

让公众深信他们的“上级”只会做符合公众最大利益的事，即使没人能确切知道，这简直就是现实版的赫胥黎《美丽新世界》。

children.author: nvme0n1p1
children.textRawHtml:
> I’m genuinely confused at how it caught on

Probably because they said AI rewrote it in 11 days, yet haven't cut a release almost 2 months later. If their AI finished it, where's the release?

They ported enough of it to run a single app (Claude Code). Good job. But if I ported Linux to Rust and it was only capable of running a single app, should I be able say it was a complete port? We'd all agree that was misleading. It's the same with Bun.

The marketing lies simply backfired.
children.textZhHtml:
> 我真的很困惑它是怎么传播开来的

可能是因为他们说 AI 在 11 天内就重写了它，但将近两个月过去了却还没有发布版本。如果他们的 AI 完成了重写，那版本在哪呢？

他们移植了足够多的代码来运行一个单一的应用（Claude Code）。干得不错。但如果我把 Linux 移植到 Rust，却只能运行一个应用，我能说这是一次完整的移植吗？我们都会认为这是误导。Bun 的情况也一样。

营销谎言简直适得其反。

children.author: simonw
children.textRawHtml:
> If their AI finished it, where's the release?

Producing a stable release for their community of code that had been written by AI in 11 days and had not yet been extensively tested in the real world would be grossly irresponsible.

Instead, they made the AI rewrite available as a canary release and shipped it for a month as part of Claude Code to millions of their own users.
children.textZhHtml:
> 如果他们的 AI 完成了重写，那版本在哪呢？

对于社区而言，将 AI 在 11 天内编写且尚未在真实环境中经过广泛测试的代码直接作为稳定版发布，是极其不负责任的。

相反，他们将 AI 重写的版本作为金丝雀发布版提供，并作为 Claude Code 的一部分向数百万用户推送测试了一个月。

children.author: nvme0n1p1
children.textRawHtml:
So... not finished, then? There have been lots of commits between then and now.

If I pay someone to build a house and they left me a voicemail saying "Yep the house is finished, it only took us 11 days!" And then later, "No, you can't move in yet, still fixing some last-minute issues (there's no plumbing yet)." We would classify this as: a lie. And if you told it to your investors: fraud.

Would it really be so bad for Anthropic to admit that a project of this size takes months instead of weeks?

I'm not saying AI is not capable of this. I'm saying that their dishonest marketing has given ammo to their haters.
children.textZhHtml:

Anthropic承认这种规模的项目需要几个月而不是几周，真的有那么难吗？

我并不是说人工智能做不到这一点。我是说他们不诚实的营销给他们的反对者提供了弹药。

children.author: johnfn
children.textRawHtml:
> If their AI finished it, where's the release?

`bun upgrade --canary`. You can use it today.

Keeping a large release, like a total rewrite, on canary for a while to iron out bugs is a very reasonable software engineering practice.

I guess that's why is an active research area, and an interdisciplinary one, what is intelligence? Is what have you practiced a ton of times? Is what you have purposely and efficiently practice? So what should you cull and how much? There's already techniques in CNNs to trim unused or less active neuron paths to reduce a model's size, but how do you (and how much) do it in a general LLM? A product that will be used without supervision from a child to an 80yo elder?

children.textRawHtml:
I've been dealing with it on the post-training (runtime) side with a large codebase that contains many moving parts, many rules and requirements. Putting all of that into the context has already gone far past 1MB, so it's untenable.

Now I have all of that information stored in a pointers-to-resources fashion, where layers of small "directories" of triggers-to-information point the agent gradually towards deeper, more esoteric knowledge the more specific its needs become when tackling a goal.
children.textZhHtml:
我一直在训练后（运行时）方面使用包含许多移动部件、许多规则和要求的大型代码库来处理它。将所有这些内容放入上下文中已经远远超过了 1MB，因此是站不住脚的。

现在，我以指向资源的指针的方式存储所有这些信息，其中触发信息的小“目录”层将代理逐渐指向更深、更深奥的知识，在解决目标时，其需求变得越具体。

stories.title: The coolest use for the Vision Pro

comments.author: jondiggsit
comments.textRawHtml:
My team uses this technology on a daily basis at my company. I run a design / build firm in the Hamptons, USA. We start all of our design projects with a 3d-first approach. Schematic design starts in 3D using Rhino3D or Revit. We use visualization plugins, like Enscape, to render the models and stream to a Quest 3 headset.

So when clients come in, and feels adventurous, we'll setup the headset, set the display height to their actual, and let them walk around their beautiful new home.

The response has been powerful. My clients are able to truly understand the scale, the proportion of rooms, ceiling heights, and the smallest details.

We're able to make real-time changes to the model (within reason) and provide instant design feedback.

I've been using this technology for years and I'm surprised it's not being adopted faster - good for us right now though!
comments.textZhHtml:
我的团队每天在我的公司使用这项技术。我在美国汉普顿经营一家设计/建造公司。我们以 3D 优先的方法开始所有设计项目。使用 Rhino3D 或 Revit 以 3D 形式开始原理图设计。我们使用 Enscape 等可视化插件来渲染模型并传输到 Quest 3 耳机。

因此，当客户进来并感到有冒险精神时，我们将设置耳机，将显示高度设置为他们的实际高度，然后让他们在美丽的新家周围走动。

反应非常强烈。我的客户能够真正了解规模、房间比例、天花板高度和最小的细节。

我们能够对模型进行实时更改（在合理范围内）并提供即时设计反馈。

我已经使用这项技术多年，但我很惊讶它没有被更快地采用 - 不过现在对我们来说有好处！

children.author: hunterpayne
children.textRawHtml:
You want a proposal? Make a kids-only set of sites. And then make hardware/software that can access only those sites. Make sure existing and future "non-kid" hardware can't access those kids-only sites. You can allow companies to register that they are one of these kid friendly sites with the additional regulation that would entail. Then make a kid having hardware that can access the normal Internet like having a beer in the US. Now perhaps you can find a hole in this, but it can be patched with technology and the right regulation.

That we aren't doing something like this gives the game away. How the EU is going about this means the point of all of this has nothing to do with children and everything to do with controlling political speech.

PS Yea, I know its a very vague suggestion, it can still be implemented

我们没有做这样的事情就暴露了游戏的本质。 欧盟的做法意味着这一切的重点与儿童无关，而与控制政治言论有关。

children.author: kelseyfrog
children.textRawHtml:
You have to stop thinking like an engineer and start thinking like a public health official.

'Something impossible for kids to bypass' is not the goal. It's akin to evaluating a flu vaccine on the standard of zero breakthrough cases. Such a standard has no relevance on the efficacy of the vaccine.

Likewise for underage internet access. Proponents would be happily satisfied with 90% compliance. They really don't care that coverage isn't complete or circumvention is complete. Once you realize that, you can start constructing counterarguments that dismantle the claim that digital IDs would solve the problems they're supposed to.
children.textZhHtml:
你必须停止像工程师一样思考，而开始像公共卫生官员一样思考。

“孩子们无法绕过的东西”不是目标。这类似于以零突破病例的标准来评估流感疫苗。这样的标准与以下内容无关：疫苗的功效。

未成年人上网也是如此。支持者会对 90% 的遵守率感到高兴。他们真的不在乎覆盖不完整或规避是否完整。一旦你意识到这一点，你就可以开始构建反驳，驳斥数字身份证可以解决其应有问题的说法。

The last time I had police knocking at my door, it was a lot more than two, and they were readying their battering ram when I opened, and then immediately swarmed me and told me to sit down, and then I just explained and they realized their warrant was for a different address and they left. It was scary in the moment, but I never had a gun pointed at me and I wasn't even touched, so overall it left me with a rather positive impression of how search warrants are executed in Germany.

By all means, if you have an adversarial relationship with the state, fight every expansion of its power tooth and nail. But conversely, if you think that everything is going basically fine and the police are reasonable folks overall, then giving them more power doesn't look like a slippery slope straight to dystopia.

I went through the same on my 10-inch Android tablet. The key is just sticking with it long enough to get it set up for your needs and prefs. I'm glad I did because it's really great. Once I got familiar with the main flow of the UI, it hasn't been an issue for my daily-use needs. If you care about flexibility, control, features and having it "your way", I think it's well worth the one-time effort to set up. children.author: incanus77
children.textRawHtml:
> Most OSS software favors power users instead of total beginners. And even Blender is not a great exercise in discoverability. You need training to use it.

I think it’s more subtle than that. I am a power user — I was compiling my Linux kernel in the 90s, I wrote my own SSH tunnel manager 20 years ago, I always fiddle with settings, etc. etc.

However, I am constantly frustrated with a lot of OSS software because it expects you to think like the developer of the tool, instead of having empathy for the user. What feels obvious to the developer of the tool (I am making up a hopefully-representative hypothetical here, but finding the change of font under “Theme” because it’s how “it looks” but finding the font size under “View” because, well, you view it) feels frustrating and nonsensical to a normal human who relates both the font and its size the same way in their mind. When I switched to the Mac in 2002, it is because these sorts of things made sense. children.author: horsawlarway
children.textRawHtml:
I find this is mostly just a "mindset" difference.

OSS software aligns mentally with "tool". It only exists because someone had a problem to solve, and they wanted a tool to solve it. Generally, people should expect to have to learn how to use tools. Then they solve their problem and move on. It takes effort, and the result is mastery which gives you new capabilities.

Consumer software (and especially anything ad supported or social media adjacent, and sadly in many respects, lots of modern SaaS companies) want to be as glitzy and smooth as possible, but they don't actually want you to solve your problem. Instead they'd really prefer that you simply spend as much time looking at their software as possible. So the experience can be quite pleasant, it feels nice, things feel obvious, you get the dopamine hits quick and fast. But after a while you realize you aren't actually all that productive (or even productive at all) when engaging with them. Because the goal of this software isn't to help you solve your problem. The goal is to keep your attention and extract your money. If it happens to solve your problem... sometimes that's fine, sometimes that's actually counter to the primary mission of extracting your time and money.
children.textZhHtml:
我发现这主要只是“心态”差异。

stories.title: AI's top startups are barely publishing their research
stories.titleZh: 人工智能领域的头部初创企业极少发表研究成果。

comments.author: ninjahawk1
comments.textRawHtml:
I can’t speak for other startups, but I applied to the most recent YC batch with my idea for making AI proactive instead of reactive, and pre-being selected I’ve published a paper on recursive self-improvement mapped to the Epoch AI data.

I contacted a professor from a university in the UK and he responded since he was working on similar work, then asked me if I wanted to meet with him. We talked for about an hour since we had overlapping results and different methods, specifically different assumptions.

I say all that to say, as a physics student getting my undergrad, simply doing independent research and speaking to experts about it enabled me to network with someone I otherwise likely wouldn’t know. For young people getting into any business, research is a great way to meet new people.
comments.textZhHtml:
我无法代表其他初创公司发言，但我带着让AI从被动转为主动的想法申请了最新一期的YC，并且在入选前，我已经发表了一篇关于递归自我改进并映射到Epoch AI数据的论文。

我联系了一位英国大学的教授，他回复了我，因为他也在做类似的研究，然后问我想不想和他见个面。我们聊了大约一个小时，因为我们的研究结果有重合，但方法不同，特别是假设不同。

我说这些是想表达，作为一名正在读本科的物理系学生，仅仅通过做独立研究并与专家交流，就能让我结识否则可能永远不会认识的人。对于刚进入任何行业的年轻人来说，做研究是结识新人的绝佳途径。

children.author: sillysaurusx
children.textRawHtml:
That's also a reason the big labs stopped. Publishing is most valuable to people who have no other way to get the attention of smart strangers. Once you can hire nearly anyone and everyone already returns your calls, the main remaining effect of publishing is to tell your competitors which things worked.

This is what happens to every field as it turns from a science into an industry. Chemists published freely until dyes started being worth money, and then the interesting work moved into company labs and stopped coming out.
children.textZhHtml:
这也是大型实验室停止公开论文的原因之一。发表论文对那些没有其他途径引起聪明陌生人注意的人来说最有价值。一旦你能雇佣几乎任何人，而且每个人都会回复你的电话，那么发表论文剩下的主要作用就是告诉竞争对手哪些方法奏效了。

这是每个领域从科学转变为产业时都会发生的现象。化学家们曾自由地发表论文，直到染料开始变得值钱，然后有趣的研究就转移到了公司实验室里，不再对外公布了。

There's already an RPL, incidentally: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Reciprocal_Public_License

Even the GPL is kind of in a gray area because the virality feature and its definition of "derivative work" have never been tested in court, to my knowledge. Maybe under contract law, no idea. children.author: fc417fc802
children.textRawHtml:
Well it was a joke and is obviously quite silly but I believe it would be enforceable to the extent that the licensor could terminate the agreement and sue for damages. If I can agree to pay you not to talk about something (ie an NDA) or not to work in a field (ie a non-compete clause) then why can't I pay you to be required to publish all future work you do in a given area? ("All future work" might well be overly broad; you'd likely have to restrict it to only a few years but I'm no lawyer.)

I don't believe the GPL is in a grey area. When you license a work all sorts of strings are commonly attached. Rather IIUC no one has gone out of the way to test the GPL largely because it is clearly within bounds, plus any violation has the potential to be a PR disaster since violations are quite literally examples of looting the commons.
children.textZhHtml:
嗯，这是一个笑话，显然很愚蠢，但我相信只要许可方可以终止协议并起诉损害赔偿，它就可以强制执行。如果我可以同意付钱给你，让你不要谈论某件事（即保密协议）或不在某个领域工作（即非竞争条款），那么为什么我不能付钱给你，要求你发布你在特定领域未来所做的所有工作？ （“所有未来的工作”可能过于宽泛；您可能不得不将其限制在几年内，但我不是律师。）

我不认为 GPL 处于灰色地带。当您获得作品许可时，通常会附加各种条件。相反，IIUC 没有人特意测试 GPL，主要是因为它显然在范围内，而且任何违规行为都有可能成为公关灾难，因为违规行为毫不夸张是掠夺公共资源的例子。

children.author: fluoridation
children.textRawHtml:
>terminate the agreement

Meaning what? Claw back the ideas from people's minds? You can terminate the agreement in the sense that you revoke access to the paper, but presumably the person you find in breach has already used the research for something that you find them in breach for. You're kind of closing the gate after the horse has bolted.

>sue for damages

I honestly have no idea what damages you could claim from not publishing research. I think you would need to set a value ahead of time on the agreement.

>If I can agree to pay you not to talk about something (ie an NDA) or not to work in a field (ie a non-compete clause) then why can't I pay you to be required to publish all future work you do in a given area?

Not sure why you added the word "pay" to your clauses, but anyway. The reason is that the existing contracts have well-defined boundaries. An NDA stops you from divulging a very specific set of information. A non-compete clause stops you from working in a very specific field. Your proposal has an undefined reach. What counts as research? What counts as "related"? It would seem that if I agree to such a contract, my entire life, both private and professional, after reading the paper is covered by the contract, and anything I do might come under scrutiny. There's never a point when I can go off-duty. "What's that? You read my paper on compression and were working on a side-project that uses compression? Gonna have to see some publication on it."

>Rather IIUC no one has gone out of the way to test the GPL largely because it is clearly within bounds

No, it's because the status quo is convenient and no one wants to be the first guinea pig. It's definitely not obvious that the terms are legally valid, but it's ambiguous enough that people don't want to test it.
children.textZhHtml:
>终止协议

什么意思？从人们的头脑中夺回想法？您可以终止协议，即撤销对论文的访问权限，但您发现违规者可能已经将研究成果用于您发现他们违规的用途。你就像是在马儿逃跑后关上大门。

>起诉损害赔偿

老实说，我不知道你可以因为不发表研究而索赔什么损害赔偿。我认为您需要提前在协议上设定一个价值。

>如果我可以同意支付您不谈论某事（即保密协议）或不在某个领域工作（即非竞争条款）的费用，那么为什么我不能支付您在特定领域发布您未来所做的所有工作的费用？

不知道为什么您在条款中添加了“支付”一词，但无论如何。原因是现有合同有明确的界限。保密协议可阻止您泄露一组非常具体的信息。竞业禁止条款会阻止您在特定领域工作。您的提案的范围尚未明确。什么才算是研究？什么才算“相关”？看来，如果我同意这样一份合同，我的整个生活，无论是私人的还是职业的，在读完这篇论文后都将受到合同的保护，我所做的任何事情都可能受到审查。我从来没有可以下班的时候。 “那是什么？你读了我关于压缩的论文，并且正在研究一个使用压缩的副项目？你一定要看看一些关于它的出版物。”

>相反，IIUC 没有人特意测试 GPL，主要是因为它显然在范围内

不，这是因为现状很方便，没有人想成为第一个小白鼠。这些条款是否具有法律效力绝对不明显，但它的含糊性足以让人们不想测试它。

children.author: fc417fc802
children.textRawHtml:
> Meaning what? Claw back the ideas ...

If something is so obviously wrong then perhaps take a minute to consider that your interpretation isn't what the other party intended?

If I pay you not to do something and then you breach the contract I can terminate the agreement and seek damages. Ditto if I pay you to repeatedly do something and then at some point you fail to do it. So if I pay you a recurring fee to publish all your research on a given topic and then you fail to make good on that I can seek damages, right? Now what if I paid you a lump sum up front? Now what if I licensed a patent to you in place of that lump sum? What if instead of a patent it was the right to make use of a piece of software?

> I honestly have no idea what damages you could claim from not publishing research.

Aside from whatever was stipulated for breach of contract I expect it would be extremely situational. I agree that you'd probably want to stipulate a penalty ahead of time. The original idea was a two sentence joke after all ...

> Not sure why you added the word "pay" to your clauses

To put this into game theory lingo, I think this is because the “branching factor” for any kind of research or exploit is extremely large. So looking backwards it doesn’t seem complicated, but looking forwards there are an enormous number of possible next actions.

Similar to finding a filament for lightbulbs, it might seem obvious to use tungsten, but at the time it wasn’t and Edison searched thousands of materials.
children.textZhHtml:
用博弈论术语来说，我认为这是因为任何类型的研究或利用的“分支因素”都非常大。因此，回顾过去，这似乎并不复杂，但展望未来，下一步可能采取的行动有大量。

与寻找灯泡灯丝类似，使用钨似乎是显而易见的，但当时情况并非如此，爱迪生搜索了数千种材料。

我认为这些模型确实在发挥它们的长处；在极其庞大的数据语料库中进行不知疲倦的搜索。人类并不特别擅长这个（事实上，人类在这方面简直糟透了）。

我们在许多方面仍然具有竞争力和优势，并不是因为我们能瞬间筛选海量数据，而是因为我们能够学习、建立关联，并拥有更优的启发式方法。

在我自己的使用中，我发现AI非常擅长发现那些最终看来微不足道、但需要搜索一系列错综复杂的关联文件的漏洞。这对人类来说很耗时。

恐怕还得发生更多数据泄露事件，AI圈的人才会真正重视起来，但在很大程度上，我完全不同情他们。把自己卖给Anthropic或OpenAI，你该清楚自己签的是什么卖身契

children.author: nomel
children.textRawHtml: I think it's all based on ease. I also think that, eventually, everyone will just move to containerized AI, with a dropbox like system to get things in and out, and some fairly minimal network access. This is close to how 99% of people use AI already, through apps like the ChatGPT app.
children.textZhHtml: 我认为这一切都是基于易用性。我还认为，最终大家都会转向容器化AI，配备类似Dropbox的系统来导入导出数据，并只保留极少的网络访问权限。这已经非常接近99%的人目前使用AI的方式了，也就是通过ChatGPT应用这样的应用程序。

children.author: paulfitz
children.textRawHtml: That Dropbox like system is literally all these worms need to propagate.
children.textZhHtml: 类似 Dropbox 的系统实际上就是这些蠕虫病毒传播所需要的。

children.author: HlessClaudesman
children.textRawHtml: So everybody has their own AI, running in a literal cave, with zero data ingress or egress. Perfection.
children.textZhHtml: 所以每个人都拥有自己的AI，在名副其实的山洞里运行，数据零进零出。简直完美。

children.author: whaleofatw2022
children.textRawHtml: Its funny because I have been asked by some folks at work as to why I dont just 'allow all commands' and instead review each one, and then I let my colleague in infosec know who asks that so they are aware of dangerous users.
children.textZhHtml: 这挺搞笑的，因为公司里有些人问我为什么不直接“允许所有命令”而是要逐一审查，然后我就让信息安全部门的同事留意一下问这种问题的人，好让他们知道哪些是危险用户。

children.author: HlessClaudesman
children.textRawHtml: It's always the ones you most suspect.
children.textZhHtml: 它始终是您最怀疑的。

children.author: inigyou
children.textRawHtml: The user wants to reformat his hard drive. I can use the bash tool for this. Wait, does the user want a full reformat or just deletion of all files? Ah, the user only wants to delete his home directory. I can do this with the command "rm -rf $HOME" using the bash tool.
children.textZhHtml: 用户想要重新格式化他的硬盘。我可以用bash工具来做这个。等等，用户是想完全格式化还是只删除所有文件？啊，用户只是想删除他的主目录。我可以用bash工具通过“rm -rf $HOME”命令来完成这个操作。

children.author: denkmoon
children.textRawHtml:
Nobody cares. Nobody with the power to do anything about itcares because they don't bare the costs.

You can see this pre AI with how companies handle data breaches. They never cared about security outside of reducing financial liability. Why would they let such petty concerns, which they are already insulated to the hilt against with all the well practiced liability reducing procedures and checklists, prevent them from capitalising on "massive productivity gains"?
children.textZhHtml:
没人在乎。任何有权力采取措施的人都不在乎，因为他们不用承担代价。

在AI出现之前，看看公司是如何处理数据泄露的就知道了。除了降低财务责任外，他们从来不关心安全问题。他们怎么会允许这种微不足道的问题——他们早就用各种熟练的免责程序和检查清单把自己武装到了牙齿——来阻碍他们利用“巨大的生产力提升”来牟利呢？

children.author: MichaelZuo
children.textRawHtml: There are a lot of fake people who claim they highly prioritize data security but in fact do not…
children.textZhHtml: 有很多假人声称他们高度重视数据安全，但实际上并没有......

children.author: voakbasda
children.textRawHtml: The product may change with the times, but there will always be snake oil salesman.
children.textZhHtml: 产品或许会与时俱进，但江湖骗子永远存在。

children.author: yifanl
children.textRawHtml: We're back to Von Neumann architecture in the worst way possible.
children.textZhHtml: 我们又回到了冯·诺依曼架构，而且是以最糟糕的方式。

children.author: cwmoore
children.textRawHtml: We’ve jumped from object-oriented to subject-oriented
children.textZhHtml: 我们已经从面向对象跃升至面向主题

children.author: SV_BubbleTime
children.textRawHtml: Subjectively subject oriented.
children.textZhHtml: 主观上以主体为导向。

children.author: Joker_vD
children.textRawHtml: Yes, the one where the program counter also doubles as the only index register available, so you process data by executing it, hopefully in a somewhat "inert" state of mind.
children.textZhHtml: 是的，程序计数器还兼作唯一可用的索引寄存器，因此您可以通过执行数据来处理数据，希望处于某种“惰性”的心态中。

children.author: xpct
children.textRawHtml: It's probably fuzzily fixable by including instruction authority levels in the training data. Can't expect much more than that, given that the model itself is fuzzy.
children.textZhHtml: 通过在训练数据中加入指令权限级别，或许能模糊地修复这个问题。考虑到模型本身就是模糊的，也不能指望更多了。

children.author: veganmosfet
children.textRawHtml: I think this is already implemented and called message roles: system, user, tool and assistant (ordered by authority). Untrusted data shall only be injected in tool responses, which are less authoritative. But at the end, this all ends in the big token stream - so this is not a perfect separation.
children.textZhHtml: 我认为这已经实现并称为消息角色：系统、用户、工具和助手（按权限排序）。不受信任的数据只能注入到工具响应中，其权威性较低。但最终，这一切都以大代币流结束——所以这不是一个完美的分离。

children.author: HlessClaudesman
children.textRawHtml: What would non fuzzy AI look like? Seems to me the fuzzyness is where all the fun is.
children.textZhHtml: 非模糊人工智能会是什么样子？在我看来，模糊性才是所有乐趣所在。

children.author: QuercusMax
children.textRawHtml: We've already seen that it's possible to trick models into seeing user input as their own "thinking" if you make it sound like what the model writes. While it may appear that it's looking at the tags on the input, in practice that's not as strong a guarantee as you'd hope.
children.textZhHtml: 我们已经看到，如果你让它听起来像模型所写的那样，就有可能欺骗模型将用户输入视为自己的“想法”。虽然它可能看起来它正在查看输入上的标签，但实际上这并不像您希望的那样强有力的保证。
